Learned advocate Ms. Karuna Rahevar waives service of notice of Admission for and on behalf of the respondent No.2.
With the consent of learned advocate appearing for the respective parties, present appeal is taken up for final hearing.

[1.0] Present First Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "MV Act") is filed by the appellant - original claimant challenging the impugned judgment and award dated 31.12.2021 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi.), at Deesa (for short "learned Tribunal") in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.2667/2009 (Old No.527/2003), whereby the learned Tribunal was pleased to partly allow the claim petition and awarded compensation of Navinbhai Trikmabhai Kag(Patel) vs Bhanvarsing Ganeshaji Rao(Barot) on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172070345/
1 Rs.4,51,898/- to the appellant - original claimant NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3371/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined after deducting 20% towards negligence of the claimant from total amount of Rs.5,64,872/-.
[2.0] The brief facts leading to filing of present appeal are as follows:
[2.1] On 03.04.1999, the appellant - claimant was going from village Kunvarla to village Dhanera by driving his owned Vehicle Scooter bearing No.GJ-8-E-5382 with moderate speed and on it's correct side by following the traffic rules and when the said Scooter was passing on the edge of bridge of river which is situated on the road leading from village Thavar to village Dhanera, Jeep bearing No.GJ-8-D-7141 came from the opposite side in full speed in rash and negligent manner endangering human life and as a result of that, the driver of the Jeep lost control over steering of the Jeep and coming on wrong side dashed with the scooter of the appellant and thus,
the accident occurred due to which the appellant sustained serious bodily injuries and therefore, the appellant - original claimant initially filed claim petition under Section 163-A of the MV Act which was subsequently converted into claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act.

sentences.text: [2.2] After considering the evidence produced and adduced, the learned Tribunal held the driver of Jeep to be 80% negligent and the appellant - original claimant - scooterist to be 20% contributory negligent for the accident
and awarded compensation of Rs.4,51,898/- to the appellant - original claimant after deducting 20% towards his own negligence, from total amount of Rs.5,64,872/-.
Hence, present appeal is filed by the appellant - original claimant challenging the contributory negligence of 20% held on the part of the claimant as well as for enhancement of compensation.

[3.0] Learned advocate Mr. Kaash Thakkar appearing for the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3371/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined appellant - original claimant has submitted that the learned Tribunal has committed an error in considering 20% contributory negligence on the part of the claimant without considering the panchnama in its true perspective.

He has further submitted that perusing the record, it appears that offending vehicle Jeep was solely negligent in causing the accident and therefore, has requested to hold the jeep driver to be solely negligent for the accident considering the doctrine of 'contributory negligence' which has replaced the old English doctrine of 'last opportunity'.

He has further argued that the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate that merely driving a vehicle or being behind the steering wheel is itself not a reason to presume contributory negligence and it must be proved by evidence that the person driving was negligent in causing the accident.

In this regard, he has relied on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Jiju Kuruvila & Ors vs Kunjujamma Mohan & Ors reported in (2013) 9 SCC 166 and Ashwinbhai Modi vs. Ramkaran Sharma reported in 2014 ACJ 2648 and submitted that even the jeep driver has not stepped into the witness box and hence,

Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 is not considered by the learned Tribunal as the claimant was entitled to 40% addition towards future prospects.

sentences.text: Further, he has argued that the learned Tribunal has not properly awarded compensation under the head of medical expenses and though the claimant incurred medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,50,000/-, learned Tribunal awarded only NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3371/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined Rs.1,00,000/- under the said head.
Even, under other heads, meager compensation is awarded though 48% disability was sustained by the claimant.
Hence, he has requested to allow the appeal.

[4.0] Learned advocate Ms. Karuna Rahevar appearing for the respondent No.2 - insurance company has opposed the present appeal by submitting that the learned Tribunal has rightly held the appellant - original claimant - scooterist 20%
contributory negligence for the accident and has awarded just and proper compensation which does not call for any interference by this Court.
Hence, she has requested to dismiss the first appeal.
[5.0] As the present appeal is filed challenging the contributory negligence on the part of original claimant and quantum of compensation, present appeal is considered in narrow compass.

[6.0] Having heard learned advocate for the appellant - original claimant and learned advocate for the respondent No.2 - insurance company and perusing the record, it appears that initially claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of the MV Act and subsequently converted into one under Section 166 of the MV Act without joining driver of offending jeep as party though complaint was filed by the jeep driver and his name was known to the claimant though the claimant has not joined the jeep driver as party in the claim petition and only owner of jeep was joined before the learned Tribunal.

[6.1] The claimant has deposed before the Tribunal that the driver of offending jeep was negligent and in order to prove the claim, the claimant has tendered evidence by way of affidavit and in the cross- examination conducted by the insurance company,
the claimant has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3371/2024 JUDGMENT DATED:
05/03/2026 undefined stated that both the vehicles collided head on and that his scooter was on correct side of the road and the jeep dashed with his scooter.

Perusing the complaint (Exh.76), which is filed by the jeep driver, it appears that it has been clearly stated in the complaint that the scooter was coming from opposite direction Navinbhai Trikmabhai Kag(Patel) vs Bhanvarsing Ganeshaji Rao(Barot) on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172070345/
3 and both the vehicles dashed and therefore, involvement of both the vehicles in the accident is not in dispute.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimant has admitted in his cross- examination that he was shifted to hospital by the jeep driver for his treatment.
Further, panchnama of scene of accident (Exh.77) reveals that width of road is 20 feet and there was a turn at the place of accident.

Considering the size of vehicles as well as damage caused to both the vehicles, it appears that front portion of the scooter of the claimant including its head light is badly damaged and even dent is found on the middle portion of bull bar of the jeep.

Hence, it appears that there was a head on collision and therefore, it was the responsibility of driver of both the vehicles to drive their respective vehicles with proper care and caution and keeping in mind expected and unexpected circumstances that may arise while driving the vehicles.

Hence,
considering the principle of res ipsa loquitur learned Tribunal in light of the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi vs. H.R.S.T.C. reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819 and Parmeshwari Devi vs. Amir Chand reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has properly appreciated the evidence and committed no error in holding the jeep driver to be 80% negligent and appellant - original claimant - scooterist to be 20% contributory negligent in causing the accident.

sentences.text: [7.0] Initially, the claimant was shifted to C.H.C. Dhanera and injury certificate issued by the said hospital is produced at Exh.80.

It appears from the record that initially the claimant was treated by Dr. Shreekant Gupta, M.S. (Ortho) for fracture of right femur, fracture of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3371/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined right radius ulna and fracture of left radius & ulna.

Further, the X-ray report of the claimant dated 19.02.2002 shows fracture of shaft femur of right side and fracture of radius and injury certificate of Dhanera Civil Hospital also say fracture of left forearm and wound on right thigh and medical paper dated 11.05.1999 shows fracture of femur and surgery of ulna radius and therefore, it is apparent on record that the claimant sustained fracture injuries on left and right forearm and on right thigh.

Further, Dr. Mahesh Khandelwal, M.S.(Ortho), who has not treated the patient, has issued the disability certificate (Exh.49) wherein 57.8%
permanent disability is assessed.

But, insurer has already admitted 48% permanent disability body as a whole of the claimant and therefore, no further discussion is required more particularly in view of the admission on the part of the insurance company in light of section 58 of the Indian Evidence Act.
Hence, aspect of disability is not discussed further.
[7.1] Further, the income tax return for the AY 01.01.1998 to 31.03.1999 is produced at Exh.48 wherein annual income of the claimant is mentioned as Rs.38,006/- from business source.

Hence, business income of the claimant is assessed at Rs.3,168/- per month and considering the agricultural income on the basis of evidence produced at Exhs.56 and 57 i.e. village abstract 7/12 and 8/A respectively, the learned Tribunal has considered supervisory and managerial loss and since claimant was engaged in business, in addition to the income from business, Rs.1000/- per month is considered as income from agriculture work and

thus, the learned Tribunal has Navinbhai Trikmabhai Kag(Patel) vs Bhanvarsing Ganeshaji Rao(Barot) on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172070345/
4 considered total monthly income of claimant at Rs.4,200/-, which does not call for any interference by this Court.
[7.2] The claimant has produced the school leaving certificate at NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3371/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined Exh.50 wherein birth date of claimant is mentioned as 27.02.1964 and therefore, on the date of accident i.e. on 03.04.1999, the claimant was aged 35 years and therefore, in view of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Smt. Sarla Verma & Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the learned Tribunal has rightly considered the multiplier of 16, which does not call for any interference.

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Verma & Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, the learned Tribunal has not considered future prospects but as the claimant was aged 35 years, in view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Shethi (Supra), 40% i.e.
Rs.1680/- (40% of Rs.4200/-) towards future prospect is required to be added and thus, the amount of monthly future loss of income would come to Rs.5880/- (Rs.4200 + Rs.1680).
Hence, applying the multiplier of 16, the appellant would be entitled to Rs.11,28,960/- (Rs.5880 x 12 x 16) towards future loss of income.
To that extent the learned Tribunal has committed an error.

[7.3] So far as medical expenses is concerned, medical bills are produced at Exhs.45, 46 and 48 for a total amount of Rs.1,50,952/- but Bill No.406 dated 05.04.1999 mentions operation charges as Rs.5,000/- with other expenses.

Further, Bill No.414 dated 19.04.1999 mentions operation charge Rs.7,500/- and another Bill No.466 dated 31.08.1999 mentions operation charge as Rs.4,250/- and Bill No.550 mentions operation charge as Rs.4,000/- and another bill No.652 dated 26.06.2000 mentions operation charge as Rs.5,000/- and therefore, according to Bill Nos.406, 414, 466, 550 and 652 total 5 times operation charges are charged and therefore, total five times, the claimant was operated while Exhs.50A, 51, 52, 54 and 55, which are medical papers of Dr.Shreekant Gupta show that only three times operation was carried out and therefore, considering variation in the bill amounts, learned Tribunal has awarded lump sum amount of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3371/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical bills though bills for an amount of Rs.1,50,952/- were produced.

Though the learned Tribunal has not committed any error in awarding Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses but in the considered opinion of this Court, considering documents produced at Exhs.45, 46, 51, 52, 54, 55 and 58,
without discussing further, it would be just and proper to award Rs.1,25,000/- under the head of medical expenses.

[7.4] So far as compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal under different other heads namely pain, shock and suffering, actual loss of income and transportation and special diet is concerned, in the considered opinion of this Court, no error has been committed and learned Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation under the said heads, which does not call for any interference.

However, so far as compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head of loss of amenities is concerned, this Court is of considered opinion that in view of compensation reassessed under the head of future loss of income, no compensation is required to be awarded under the head of loss of amenities.

[8.0] As discussed above, the appellant - original claimant is entitled to get compensation computed as under:

Thus, total compensation of Rs.5,64,872/- as awarded by the learned Tribunal is on lower side, for the reasons recorded hereinabove, and therefore, same is required to be reassessed to the aforesaid extent i.e. Rs.13,21,760/-.

However, considering 20% contributory negligence on the part of the appellant - claimant, Rs.2,64,352/- (20% of Rs.13,21,760/-) is required to be sliced down and therefore, the appellant - original claimant is entitled to Rs.10,57,408/- (Rs.13,21,760 - Rs.2,64,352)
towards reassessed compensation and therefore, the impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal is required to be modified to the aforesaid extent.
[9.0] In wake of aforesaid conspectus, present First Appeal is partly allowed.

The impugned judgment and award dated 31.12.2021 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi.), at Deesa in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.2667/2009 (Old No.527/2003) is modified and respondent No.2 is directed to deposit Rs.10,57,408/- with the learned Tribunal alongwith accrued interest and costs as awarded by the learned Tribunal within a period of FOUR WEEKS from the date of receipt of this judgment.
